Summary: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration for emphasis — a common and accepted way of speaking in the Bible's world. It is meant to shock the hearer into taking something seriously, not to be obeyed woodenly or dismissed as a joke.
HowToApply: When a statement sounds extreme, ask whether the author is using exaggeration to underline urgency or seriousness. Let the overstatement make its point, then apply the point — not the exaggerated form.
ScriptureExample: Matthew 5:29 — 'if your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out' uses shocking language to show how radical the fight against sin must be. Jesus is not commanding self-mutilation; he is commanding seriousness about holiness.
CommonMistake: Obeying hyperbole literally (and harming oneself or others) or, at the other extreme, shrugging it off as mere colorful talk and missing the urgent point entirely.
